q: ‘Hrrmph!’ said the machine-gun through all its five noses as the subaltern drew the lever home.
1891 January, Rudyard Kipling, chapter XV, in The Light that Failed, London; New York, N.Y.: Macmillan and Co., published March 1891, →OCLC, page 327:
I mustered up courage to shake the box, but not to enter the office. “bring it in” said Robin with a hrrmph!
2009, Aaron Chynn, Memoirs of an Ordinary Man: A Yorkshireman's Tale, page 49:
She lets out what starts as a sigh but finishes off as a hrrmph.
2011, Lee Stringer, Sleepaway School: Stories from a Boy's Life; A Memoir, page 151:
She rolled through the house, pushed by Baz or wheeling herself, with nothing but a scowl and a hrrmph for Willa, who had no idea what she'd done to incur the old lady's wrath.
